+title: Fix the continuation misuse in the ResilienceTests helper respawningThatHangsAfterFirstConnect
+---
+Found on ^cepemvm (2026-10-17): the full swift test log has one line "SWIFT TASK CONTINUATION MISUSE" for the test helper respawningThatHangsAfterFirstConnect in Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/ResilienceTests.swift. The runtime writes this when a checked continuation is resumed more than one time, or is released with no resume. The tests still pass, but a leaked continuation can hold a task forever (rule T1), and a double resume is a crash in some builds.
+
+Do:
+- Read the helper and find the continuation that is leaked or resumed two times. Fix it so that each continuation is resumed exactly one time on each path (a cancel and a connection end included). Use the shared TestHookWait or TestHookWaiters code if it fits.
+- Show that the warning is gone: the full swift test log has no "SWIFT TASK CONTINUATION MISUSE" line.
+- Keep the checks of each test the same. No .timeLimit, sleep, poll or retry. Do not delete a test. One full run. #elicitation-fixes #t1
\ No newline at end of file
